assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only konosuba:pickles@original-light-novel#expanded-cohort-monograph, the active_provisional KONOSUBA_PICKLES_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the YORI-01 U012 paragraph and ruby projection (P1-336). The subject is deceased and reached principally through Aqua's translation while he possesses a toy, with Eibram's corroboration; the monograph is a Tier 2 study that itself declines a behavioral reconstruction. The KonoSuba CURRENT_STATE_AND_CORPUS_MAP.md was read for method, authority order and scope only. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The single posthumous YORI-01 U012 episode, from Aqua's identification at P136-144 to the reported departure at P253 and Eibram's unanswered parentage question at P254. His life as head of the house is reported only (P139, P182, P202, P249), not narrated as a state, and no in-world calendar time is fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph's account is a gap between a maintained strict public image and suppressed wishes (P182), followed by tactical bargaining once the diary is exposed (P219-228). It explicitly declines a separate behavioral reconstruction because generic embarrassment, posthumous indulgence, status defense and the diary-reveal structure explain overlapping parts of one mediated episode.

His life is available only as reported preferences, image and an adoption disclosure, and the posthumous episode is one scene sequence; no developmental state or transition model is established. The shift after the diary is found is graded as conflict behavior.

Every utterance is Aqua's quotation or paraphrase. The monograph names printed pragmatic effects (noble/commoner contrast, direct demands, family address, insulting retreat, reward plea at P228) but states that it does not certify his delivery, original particles or a habitual register, and that Aqua's own comments must not be assigned to him. The mediation limit is recorded as an evidence-backed known limit.

Guitar, gardening and an eleven-year pink Neroid preference (P139) are Aqua-mediated facts the son recognizes. They answer a bounded canon question about reported tastes; none is performed in the scene.

The monograph differentiates his conduct toward his son (filial warmth, succession, adverse advice P233, adoption disclosure P249), the maids (embraces of the possessed toy P172-177), Darkness (requests escalating until she refuses further translation, P207-214) and Kazuma (the unperformed strike demand P195; the bargain under threat P227-228). Each rests on one mediated exchange.

Suppressed wishes toward the maids behind a strict image (P182) and the loss of a loved woman to the Dustiness family are the subject's own mediated explanations; the monograph treats them as interested reports that may explain a discrepancy, not as verified motives or acts.

Once the diary is found and Kazuma threatens public reading (P219-227), the translated response mixes an insult to the commoner, a noble-joke claim and a deferential plea backed by reward (P228); the monograph calls this a rapid tactical mixture, not a change of character. One negotiation does not establish escalation rules.

Located ethically salient choices: separating the remaining diary task from preceding play (P204), adverse advice to his son not to restrain himself toward maids (P233) and the adoption disclosure that leaves the son's parentage unanswered (P249, P254). No deliberation is shown; the monograph refuses to read moral growth or a deliberately timed escape into them.

Play through the possessed toy (P172-177, P192) and the noble-joke claim under exposure (P228) are located. The monograph keeps the requests' coercive and invasive implications and treats the joke claim as tactical, so this answers canon questions about the episode, not a humor repertoire.

One complete 336-paragraph unit projection with ruby, paragraph scope only, no image or whole-edition credit, a deceased subject accessed through an interpreter, and a monograph that itself rules out a behavioral model.

Affirmative located countercases: the son's praise of his government is interested testimony (P202); the adoption disclosure withdraws the dead-wife story without answering parentage (P249, P254); Eibram refuses the strike (P197) and Darkness refuses further translation (P207-214), so indulgence is not a universal permission; the advice is adverse counsel, not reform (P233). One project's adjudication of one episode.

Claims are bound to paragraph locators within the episode, and the monograph separates reported past from performed present and leaves the diary's fate and his departure as reported or unknown (P230-231, P253). No state of his life can be selected or dated.

scenario_readiness.note: No independently heard voice exists: every line is Aqua's translation, and the monograph declines to certify any register. Generated lines would be invention attributed through a second speaker.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The posthumous YORI-01 U012 episode, P136-P254, ending with the reported departure.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: His son Eibram, household maids, Darkness, Kazuma and Megumin, always through Aqua as interpreter.

No living-era scene, later appearance or uncurated evidence

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph states that the source is not enough for a separate behavioral reconstruction and names overlapping rival explanations it cannot discriminate; a different recipient and comparable reputation conflict would be needed. A novel situation can be checked against the located episode only.
Reported tastes exist, but no ordinary social encounter of his is narrated; readiness for one is neither supported nor denied.
Located choices show adverse advice and an unanswered disclosure without visible deliberation, and the monograph refuses to infer reform or intent; no procedure for a new ethical choice exists.

The suppressed wishes toward maids and the lost love to the Dustiness family are interested mediated reports that the monograph declines to treat as proof of an affair, entitlement or acted fantasy; they cannot condition a new romantic scene.
The former household-head role, secrecy, a hidden document and reward bargaining are located, but the monograph states that no political competence map is established.

known_limits.statement: Every Pickles utterance reaches the reader through Aqua's quotation or paraphrase while he possesses a toy; his delivery, original particles and habitual register are uncertified, and Aqua's own comments must not be assigned to him.

The son's praise of his government (P202), his own account of suppressed wishes (P182) and of a loved woman lost to the Dustiness family are interested reports; they do not establish public virtue, acted fantasies, an affair or entitlement to Darkness.
The P249 adoption disclosure withdraws the dead-wife explanation and leaves Eibram's biological parentage unanswered (P254); neither biological descent nor the absence of attachment may be inferred.
The P233 advice is adverse counsel, not moral growth or consent; the diary's destruction and contents and the completion of his departure are reported or unknown (P230-231, P253).

No narrated scene of his living life, no project reconstruction model and no uncurated readings, ledgers or Japanese source inform this assessment; missing support is not evidence that any trait or capacity is absent.
